events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the secondary high tide in the evening.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 2:15PM PST until November 20 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-19
feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from
late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and
harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to
Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea.
Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches
and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood
advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the
secondary high tide in the evening.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the secondary high tide in the evening.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 8:53PM PST until November 20 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-
19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected
from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip
currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially
to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood
advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the
secondary high tide in the evening.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do

Southeast winds could gust as high as 55 mph. * WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast. * WHEN...Until 3 PM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Snow and blowing snow could reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard conditions will be intermittently possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow arrives as winds peak Tuesday night into Wednesday. Rain may mix with snow at times Wednesday and Thursday as warmer air builds in out of the south.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Franklin County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Friday night.

weather.instruction:

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 1:25AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Eastern Clay, Eastern Putnam, Inland Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns, Northern Inland St. Johns, South Central Duval, Southeast Coastal St. Johns, Southern Inland St. Johns, Trout River, Western Clay, Western Duval, Western Putnam and Western St. Johns. * WHEN...Through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Several rounds of heavy rainfall are expected to repeatedly occur in the watch area through the end of the week. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall will result in the potential for urban and small stream flooding for the coastal areas of northeast Florida. Total rainfall forecast through Friday night is around 3 to 8 inches with locally higher amounts up to 12 inches or more. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.description: * WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to 9 PM PST Friday. Peak surf expected Thursday. * IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to 3 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous surf and coastal flooding isues are expected next week.

events.title: Winter Storm Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 and 18 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph. * WHERE...Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in Elko County. * WHEN...From midnight tonight to 4 PM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Thursday morning and evening commutes. Visibilities may drop below 1/4 mile due to falling and blowing snow.

location.region: Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 18 at 11:52AM PST until November 20 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Elko NV
weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 and
18 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in Elko County.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 4 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Thursday morning and evening
commutes. Visibilities may drop below 1/4 mile due to falling and
blowing snow.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.
weather.areaDesc: Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 10 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Southeast Georgia and Northeast Florida Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Coastal Nassau; Coastal Duval; Coastal Flagler; Northeast Coastal St. Johns; Southeast Coastal St. Johns; Coastal Glynn; Coastal Camden

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 1:41PM EST until November 22 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
10 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia and Northeast Florida Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 7:01PM PST until November 20 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-
18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is
expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous
rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially
to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through
the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous
surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 3:43AM CST until November 20 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 1:19AM EST until November 21 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia for people and animals.

location.region: North Bay Interior Mountains; North Bay Interior Valleys; Eastern Santa Clara Hills; Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo Seco and Lake San Antonio; Santa Lucia Mountains and Los Padres National Forest; Mountains Of San Benito County And Interior Monterey County Including Pinnacles National Park

weather.headline: Cold Weather Advisory issued November 19 at 10:53AM PST until November 21 at 8:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Cold conditions with temperatures between 33 and 36 degrees.

* WHERE...Interior Monterey County and the Santa Lucia Range, Most of
San Benito County and the Cholame Hills in Southeast Monterey
County, North Bay Interior Mountains, North Bay Interior Valleys,
Eastern Santa Clara Hills, and Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo Seco
and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...For the first Cold Weather Advisory, from 1 AM to 8 AM PST
Friday. For the second Cold Weather Advisory, from 1 AM to 8 AM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for
vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia
for people and animals.
weather.instruction:
Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

weather.description:

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only

surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 4:52PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 9 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored break points. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM PST Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso Bay and San
Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM
Friday and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The
Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as
Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a
Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".

property.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination with strong north-northeast flow. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are inaccessible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 3.7 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Friday was 3.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 3.8 feet. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 9:20AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Friday was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...Until 11 AM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM today and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this afternoon. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 1:46AM CST until November 20 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM CST this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 12 feet in the surf zone. * WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 12:58AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 12 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

* WHERE...Interior Monterey County and the Santa Lucia Range, Most of
San Benito County and the Cholame Hills in Southeast Monterey
County, North Bay Interior Mountains, North Bay Interior Valleys,
Eastern Santa Clara Hills, and Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo Seco
and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 8 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for
vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia
for people and animals.
weather.instruction:
Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

The effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor exercise or strenuous activity. events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in effect from 6 PM this evening to 10 AM EST Saturday. A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure. Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as much as possible. For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at: http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has issued a Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert for the Susquehanna Valley today into tonight. The periods of worst air quality will be this morning and again after sunset this evening. A Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert means that air pollution concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive groups. Sensitive groups include children, people suffering from asthma, heart disease or other lung diseases, and the elderly. The effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding strenuous activity or exercise outdoors. For more information on ground-level fine particles, visit www.airnow.gov, and www.aqpartners.state.pa.us.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 4:26PM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to continue climbing through this weekend. The river is anticipated to reach Major Flood Stage on Saturday. For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Deland. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 4.9 feet. - Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 1:30 PM EST Friday was 4.9 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet Tuesday evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter. This approaches the flood of record which is 6.3 feet. - Flood stage is 4.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 2:35PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through this weekend. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage on Saturday.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 4.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Friday was 4.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet Tuesday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter. This
approaches the flood of record which is 6.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 245 AM EST.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent observations.

currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 AM EST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. For winter road conditions from the
Utah Department of Transportation, visit
http://www.udottraffic.utah.gov.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

For graphical depictions of the snowfall forecast, including Official
NWS Forecast, High End Amount, and Low End Amount, visit
weather.gov/slc/winter.
